pull.title: MINOR: Test topic removal in the share group assignor
pull.body:
This adds explicit tests for assignments containing a topic that a
member   no longer subscribes to, covering both homogeneous and
heterogeneous   subscriptions.

- testAssignWithUnsubscribedTopicHomogeneous: two members each hold one
   partition of topic 1 and one partition of topic 2, after the group's
   subscription changes to topic 1 only. It verifies that topic 2 is
   revoked by
SimpleHomogeneousAssignmentBuilder#revokeUnassignablePartitions.

- testAssignWithUnsubscribedTopicHeterogeneous: member A drops topic 2
   while member B still subscribes to it. It verifies that A's partition
   of topic 2 is revoked and that B ends up with both partitions of
topic 2.

Topic 1 has four partitions, with only two initially assigned. Both
tests  verify that each member retains its existing partition of topic 1
and  receives one of the remaining partitions.

Reviewers: Andrew Schofield <aschofield@confluent.io>

review_comments.body: The "Incremental" tests run the assignment in a loop. This really is `testAssignWithUnsubscribedTopicHomogeneous`.

issue_comments.body:
@AndrewJSchofield Could you take a look when you have a chance? This adds a test for the topic-removal path in the homogeneous share group assignor, following your work on KAFKA-19362.

CI is awaiting approval. Could you also add the ci-approved label to allow it to run?

Testing:
- All 17 tests in SimpleAssignorTest pass.
- The new test passed in 20 repeated runs with randomly generated topic IDs.
- Removing `newMemberAssignment.remove(topicId)` from `revokeUnassignablePartitions` causes the new test to fail because topic 2 remains assigned.
- JaCoCo confirms that the topic-removal branch is exercised by the new test; it was not exercised by the existing assignor tests.

Thanks for the review, @AndrewJSchofield. I've addressed both points:

- Renamed the test to `testAssignWithUnsubscribedTopicHomogeneous`.
- Added `testAssignWithUnsubscribedTopicHeterogeneous` as its heterogeneous partner.

For the heterogeneous test I used a slightly different scenario: member A drops topic 2 while member B still subscribes to it. It checks that A's partition of topic 2 is revoked and that B ends up with both partitions of topic 2, while topic 1 is still spread two partitions per member.

I didn't mirror the homogeneous scenario exactly (no member subscribes to topic 2 anymore), because in the heterogeneous builder that case doesn't revoke topic 2. While writing the test, I tried A subscribed to {T1} and B to {T1, T3}, with both members still holding a partition of T2 in their current assignment. The result was:

    A={T2=[0], T1=[0, 2]}
    B={T2=[1], T1=[1, 3], T3=[0, 1]}

As far as I can tell, `SimpleHeterogeneousAssignmentBuilder#build` only iterates over the union of the members' subscribed topics. A topic that nobody subscribes to is never visited, so the members' old assignments for it are carried over unchanged. For the same reason, the `else` branch in `TopicAssignmentPartialBuilder#revokeUnassignablePartitions` that removes the topic seems unreachable, since `topicId` is always in `subscribedTopicIds` there.

Is this the expected behaviour? If it's a bug, I'm happy to open a JIRA and address it in a separate PR.

>

> 
> I didn't mirror the homogeneous scenario exactly (no member subscribes to topic 2 anymore), because in the heterogeneous builder that case doesn't revoke topic 2. While writing the test, I tried A subscribed to {T1} and B to {T1, T3}, with both members still holding a partition of T2 in their current assignment. The result was:
> 
> ```
> A={T2=[0], T1=[0, 2]}
> B={T2=[1], T1=[1, 3], T3=[0, 1]}
> ```
> 
> As far as I can tell, `SimpleHeterogeneousAssignmentBuilder#build` only iterates over the union of the members' subscribed topics. A topic that nobody subscribes to is never visited, so the members' old assignments for it are carried over unchanged. For the same reason, the `else` branch in `TopicAssignmentPartialBuilder#revokeUnassignablePartitions` that removes the topic seems unreachable, since `topicId` is always in `subscribedTopicIds` there.
> 
> Is this the expected behaviour? If it's a bug, I'm happy to open a JIRA and address it in a separate PR.

Yes, I think it's a bug.

> @AndrewJSchofield Thanks for confirming. Shall I open a JIRA for the heterogeneous builder keeping partitions of topics that no member subscribes to, and work on a fix in a separate PR? I'm also fine leaving it to you if you'd prefer to handle it.

@sunm2n Up to you. If you're confident attempting it, I can be the reviewer. Let me know.

> > @AndrewJSchofield Thanks for confirming. Shall I open a JIRA for the heterogeneous builder keeping partitions of topics that no member subscribes to, and work on a fix in a separate PR? I'm also fine leaving it to you if you'd prefer to handle it.
> 
> @sunm2n Up to you. If you're confident attempting it, I can be the reviewer. Let me know.

@AndrewJSchofield Thanks, I'll take it. I've opened KAFKA-21360 and will tag you on the fix PR.

While working on the fix, I noticed that the impact is limited: since KAFKA-19431, ShareGroupAssignmentBuilder filters out unsubscribed topics when reconciling the target assignment into each member's current assignment, so these stale partitions are not passed on to members. However, the stale entries remain in the stored target assignment and can survive subsequent heterogeneous rebalances. The homogeneous builder already removes them.

issue.title: KAFKA-21360: Revoke topics no member subscribes to in the heterogeneous share assignor

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
SimpleHeterogeneousAssignmentBuilder computes per-topic assignments only
for topics in the union of the members' subscriptions. As a result,
partitions of topics that no member subscribes to anymore were carried
over from the existing assignment into the new target assignment.

Revoke these topics before computing the per-topic assignments, matching
the homogeneous builder's behavior, and remove the unreachable branch in
revokeUnassignablePartitions that attempted to handle them.

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>
